name: ChemBench
intro: ChemBench 是自动化化学知识与推理评测框架，包含 2,788 道人工或半自动整理的问题，并通过主题、技能和难度标签、模型适配提示、稳健答案解析及化学专家基线比较模型能力。
org: LAMA Lab and international chemistry collaborators
build_method: 人工与半自动问题整理, 双科学家复核, 自动结构检查, 化学语义标注
task_type: 科学问答, 化学推理
eval_feature: 知识、推理、计算与直觉, 主题和难度分层, 工具增强系统, 化学专家基线
scale: 2,788道题（2,544道选择题, 244道开放题）, Mini子集236题
build_method_en: Manual and Semi-programmatic Question Curation, Two-scientist Review, Automated Schema Checks, Chemical-semantic Annotation
eval_feature_en: Knowledge, Reasoning, Calculation, and Intuition; Topic and Difficulty Stratification; Tool-augmented Systems; Chemist Baseline
intro_en: ChemBench is an automated framework for evaluating chemical knowledge and reasoning. Its 2,788 manually or semi-programmatically curated questions are labeled by topic, skill, and difficulty and evaluated through model-aware prompting, robust parsing, and comparison with chemistry experts.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with Nature Chemistry 17 (2025), Methods: Curation workflow and Model evaluation workflow, and arXiv:2404.01475. ChemBench combines 1,039 manually curated questions from novel authoring, university exams, exercises, and question banks with 1,749 semi-programmatically generated questions from curated chemical data, yielding 2,788 items: 2,544 multiple-choice and 244 open-ended. Contributions enter through GitHub pull requests in a BIG-bench-style schema with chemical semantic annotations and a BIG-bench canary string. Before merge, each item is reviewed by at least two scientists beyond the original curator and passes automated schema checks, then receives topic, skill, and difficulty labels. ChemBench-Mini selects 236 diverse questions, retains advanced items, and balances topic-skill combinations. Evaluation accepts any text-returning model or tool-augmented system, applies model-specific templates and chemical notation normalization, runs greedy decoding at temperature zero, and parses answer tags, choices, scientific numbers, and word-numbers with regex before an LLM fallback. A web survey of 19 chemistry experts on Mini provides the human baseline; results compare strict correctness and verbalized confidence and are published by topic and skill.
